title: Alexander Ovechkin announces 2026-27 will be his final NHL season
dek: The NHL's all-time leading goal-scorer, with 929 career goals, announced on Monday, October 5 that the 2026-27 season will be his 22nd and last before retirement. body: Alexander Ovechkin, the NHL's all-time leading goal-scorer, announced on Monday, October 5 that the 2026-27 season will be his 22nd and final year in the league before retirement.

Ovechkin made the announcement to his Washington Capitals teammates first, delivering the news in a video message. According to CBS Sports, he told the team: "This is gonna be my last year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun." In a statement posted on the Capitals' social media, Ovechkin said: "I love this game so much, but I know in my heart it's the right decision."

Ovechkin has recorded 929 career goals, per CBS Sports, establishing himself as the leading goal-scorer in hockey history. He was selected first overall in the 2004 NHL Draft and scored 52 goals as a rookie, winning the Calder Trophy. Over his career, Ovechkin won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the league's leading goal-scorer nine times, the Art Ross Trophy, and three Hart Trophy awards. He led Washington to the Stanley Cup championship in 2017-18, scoring 15 playoff goals and winning the Conn Smythe Trophy.

After the 2025-26 season, Ovechkin signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Capitals for his farewell campaign. The team reinforced its roster by signing former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquiring winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade, according to CBS Sports, positioning Washington for one final Stanley Cup push.
Ovechkin chose to address his teammates before the public announcement because it was important to his family that his fellow players hear the news directly from him, per Yahoo Sports reporting.

The Bottom Line: Ovechkin enters the 2026-27 season as a player in his final 82 games; the question is whether Washington's roster construction and his own performance can deliver the second championship of his career.
